legacy_record.Notes: Confirmed via Ohio Cannabis Coalition coverage: Akron-based Klutch (founder Adam Thomarios) is an active Ohio cannabis operator/brand. Documented current brand-partnership relationships, independently corroborated from two separate sources: Klutch's own June 2026 Columbus-opening press release names Cookies, Josh D and Kiva Confections directly as brand partners carried alongside Klutch's house brands (Klutch Cannabis, Citizen by Klutch, Habitat by Klutch); Klutch's Featured Brands page separately confirms the same three and additionally states Josh D has been Klutch's Ohio partner since 2018 ("OG Ohio partner"). None of the three brands are added as directory rows — see this Directory's scope note on national CPG brand-licensing entities. Also documented: an M&A/license-transfer relationship with Farkas Farms (also in this Directory) — DCC approved Klutch's June 2026 acquisition of Farkas Farms' Columbus dispensary license (5429 Bethel Sawmill Center), while Klutch simultaneously sold its Loudonville dispensary/license to Farkas Farms. Confirmed via eight independent sources including Crain's Cleveland Business. Vendor relationships, all current and confirmed via Klutch's own site: CannaPlanners (website/digital development — credited as site provider), Headset (brand-locator/data technology powering the statewide "Find Klutch Near Me" tool — narrow integration, not a broader analytics contract), Dutchie (Dutchie Pay accepted in-store), and CanPay (accepted cashless payment option). CannaPlanners, Headset, Dutchie and CanPay are all also entries in this Directory. Wholesale/distribution relationships into named current Ohio dispensary partners, per Klutch's own statewide locator: Ascend Cannabis, Amplify and Backroad Wellness (all three also entries in this Directory) are explicitly listed as current dispensary partners carrying Klutch products. The same locator names a further 17 already-listed Ohio operators as partners (Curaleaf, Elevated Growth, Ethos, Farkas Farms, Green Leaf Therapy, Greenlight, Guaranteed Dispensary, Locals, Pure Ohio Wellness, Standard Wellness, Story Cannabis, Sunnyside/Cresco, The Botanist, The Cannabist Company, The Forest, Trulieve and Verilife/PharmaCann) — recorded here rather than duplicated across 17 individual rows, since the relationship is the same in each direction (Klutch products carried at these retailers) and is fully documented by this one current source. DCC LEGAL ENTITIES: Klutch's Akron cultivation operates under AT-CPC of Ohio, LLC (CCC000042-00, -01); Bethel Sawmill Columbus under ATCL2, LLC (CCD000218-00); Wellington under related-pattern ATCL4, LLC (CCD000193-00), not independently confirmed as Klutch beyond naming pattern; Cleveland, Northfield and Akron/Tallmadge under Klutch Prospect LLC, Klutch Northfield LLC and Klutch Akron LLC; processing under Klutch Processing LLC (CCP000043-00). Address-level reconciliation now also confirms the Canton and Lorain Klutch storefronts under Citizen Real Estate, LLC / CCD000083-00 and CCD000084-00; both were formerly branded The Citizen by Klutch. SETTLED 2026 OWNERSHIP TRANSFER: On 2026-09-01 Klutch announced DCC approval to acquire Culture Cannabis Club's Grandview dispensary at 1305 Holly Ave, Columbus. Klutch's Grandview dispensary opened on 2026-09-11; the DCC legal entity remains Culture Retail Partners of Ohio, Inc. pending a roster change. 2026-11-05 review: DCC license list match; first-party site live.

Recommend a decision — keep flagged as unverified, or move out of scope like One Bond Laboratories — rather than treating this as an ordinary open contact-research row. FINAL DISPOSITION: moved out of scope rather than left open indefinitely. This is now the second independent research pass to flag the same problem — a domain-for-sale Contact page (asking $50,000+) alongside leadership bios ("John," "Emma," "Michael," "Sarah," "David," "Karen" — first names only, generic template copy) that no independent source, including Ohio-government or credible organizational records, corroborates. Two separate research passes plus this Directory's own direct check of the site all converge on the same conclusion: there is no verifiable evidence this represents a genuine operating nonprofit, as distinct from a placeholder or SEO/lead-gen site built to resemble one. evidence.value: Confirmed via Ohio Cannabis Coalition coverage: Akron-based Klutch (founder Adam Thomarios) is an active Ohio cannabis operator/brand. Documented current brand-partnership relationships, independently corroborated from two separate sources: Klutch's own June 2026 Columbus-opening press release names Cookies, Josh D and Kiva Confections directly as brand partners carried alongside Klutch's house brands (Klutch Cannabis, Citizen by Klutch, Habitat by Klutch); Klutch's Featured Brands page separately confirms the same three and additionally states Josh D has been Klutch's Ohio partner since 2018 ("OG Ohio partner"). None of the three brands are added as directory rows — see this Directory's scope note on national CPG brand-licensing entities. Also documented: an M&A/license-transfer relationship with Farkas Farms (also in this Directory) — DCC approved Klutch's June 2026 acquisition of Farkas Farms' Columbus dispensary license (5429 Bethel Sawmill Center), while Klutch simultaneously sold its Loudonville dispensary/license to Farkas Farms. Confirmed via eight independent sources including Crain's Cleveland Business. Vendor relationships, all current and confirmed via Klutch's own site: CannaPlanners (website/digital development — credited as site provider), Headset (brand-locator/data technology powering the statewide "Find Klutch Near Me" tool — narrow integration, not a broader analytics contract), Dutchie (Dutchie Pay accepted in-store), and CanPay (accepted cashless payment option). CannaPlanners, Headset, Dutchie and CanPay are all also entries in this Directory. Wholesale/distribution relationships into named current Ohio dispensary partners, per Klutch's own statewide locator: Ascend Cannabis, Amplify and Backroad Wellness (all three also entries in this Directory) are explicitly listed as current dispensary partners carrying Klutch products. The same locator names a further 17 already-listed Ohio operators as partners (Curaleaf, Elevated Growth, Ethos, Farkas Farms, Green Leaf Therapy, Greenlight, Guaranteed Dispensary, Locals, Pure Ohio Wellness, Standard Wellness, Story Cannabis, Sunnyside/Cresco, The Botanist, The Cannabist Company, The Forest, Trulieve and Verilife/PharmaCann) — recorded here rather than duplicated across 17 individual rows, since the relationship is the same in each direction (Klutch products carried at these retailers) and is fully documented by this one current source. DCC LEGAL ENTITIES: Klutch's Akron cultivation operates under AT-CPC of Ohio, LLC (CCC000042-00, -01); Bethel Sawmill Columbus under ATCL2, LLC (CCD000218-00); Wellington under related-pattern ATCL4, LLC (CCD000193-00), not independently confirmed as Klutch beyond naming pattern; Cleveland, Northfield and Akron/Tallmadge under Klutch Prospect LLC, Klutch Northfield LLC and Klutch Akron LLC; processing under Klutch Processing LLC (CCP000043-00). Address-level reconciliation now also confirms the Canton and Lorain Klutch storefronts under Citizen Real Estate, LLC / CCD000083-00 and CCD000084-00; both were formerly branded The Citizen by Klutch. SETTLED 2026 OWNERSHIP TRANSFER: On 2026-09-01 Klutch announced DCC approval to acquire Culture Cannabis Club's Grandview dispensary at 1305 Holly Ave, Columbus. Klutch's Grandview dispensary opened on 2026-09-11; the DCC legal entity remains Culture Retail Partners of Ohio, Inc. pending a roster change.

evidence.value: PL 222.05(1)(a)-(b): possession, purchase and transport of up to 3 oz cannabis and 24 g concentrated cannabis, and transfer without compensation of the same amounts, are lawful for persons 21+.
evidence.limitations: Statute text, current revision from 2021-04-02. Local rules, landlord and workplace policies are not covered. Not legal advice.

evidence.value: PL 222.15(5): up to five pounds of cannabis may be possessed in a private residence, secured from persons under 21.
evidence.limitations: Statute text, current revision from 2021-04-02. OCM home-cultivation regulations (9 NYCRR Part 115) add safety rules that are summarized only where OCM's own pages state them. Not legal advice.

evidence.value: Sharing without compensation is legal; any sale of a service or commodity tied to the sharing, including so-called gifting, is illegal. Effective date per the court system: March 31, 2021.
evidence.limitations: Agency consumer summary; it cites no statute sections.

evidence.value: PL 222.10: no smoking or vaping where prohibited under Public Health Law article 13-E, and no smoking, vaping or ingesting on school grounds or school buses; civil penalty up to $25 or up to 20 hours of community service.
evidence.limitations: Statute text, current revision from 2021-04-02. Public Health Law article 13-E smoking locations are not summarized here. Not legal advice.

evidence.value: Legal in a private home or most places tobacco can be consumed, except a motor vehicle; illegal where tobacco smoking is prohibited and on federal property.
evidence.limitations: Agency consumer summary; it cites no statute sections.

evidence.value: PL 222.15(1)-(3), (6): 3 mature and 3 immature plants per person, 6 and 6 per private residence, cultivation only at a private residence, no one under 21; localities may regulate with penalties of $200 or less but may not completely or essentially prohibit it.
evidence.limitations: Statute text, current revision from 2021-04-02. OCM home-cultivation regulations (9 NYCRR Part 115) add safety rules that are summarized only where OCM's own pages state them. Not legal advice.

evidence.value: Revised Personal Home Cultivation Regulations adopted June 11, 2024; adult-use home cultivation began June 26, 2024; no person may sell, barter or exchange cannabis without a license.
evidence.limitations: OCM adult-use home cultivation FAQ (PDF, undated; refers to rules adopted June 11, 2024 and home cultivation beginning June 26, 2024). Read through a text conversion. It does not address online, out-of-state or gifted seeds.

evidence.value: Flammable materials are prohibited for home processing; plants must be secured and odor controlled.
evidence.limitations: Agency consumer summary; it cites no statute sections.

evidence.value: Labor Law 201-d(2)(b)-(c) protects legal use of consumable products and recreational activities, including cannabis in accordance with state law, outside work hours and off premises; 201-d(4-a) permits action required by law, for articulable on-the-job impairment, or to avoid violating federal law or losing a federal contract or funding.
evidence.limitations: Statute text, current revision from 2023-09-08. Federal rules, safety-sensitive jobs and collective bargaining terms can change the outcome. Not legal advice.

evidence.value: VTL 1192(4) and (4-a) prohibit operating a motor vehicle while ability is impaired by a drug or by the combined influence of drugs or alcohol and drugs. Open Legislation shows the current revision from 2014-09-22; that date is used as the rule's effective date.
evidence.limitations: Statute text, current revision from 2014-09-22. Penalties, testing and licensing consequences are in other sections and are not summarized. Not legal advice.

evidence.value: Cannabis in a vehicle should be in a closed container; open containers and smoking in a vehicle, moving or parked, are illegal; driving under the influence is treated like alcohol-related DUI.
evidence.limitations: Agency consumer summary; it cites no statute sections.

evidence.value: Effective March 31, 2021; automatic expungement of PL 221.05, 221.10, 221.15, 221.20, 221.35, 221.40, 222.10, 222.15, 222.25 and 222.45 convictions; no notice from the court; expunged charges do not show on background checks and need not be disclosed; CPL 440.46-a motion for others.
evidence.limitations: Court-system help page. Immigration consequences and non-listed offenses need individual legal advice. Not legal advice.

evidence.value: Took effect November 16, 2024; implementation due by November 16, 2027; sex crimes and non-drug Class A felonies are not eligible.
evidence.limitations: Court-system Clean Slate page. Implementation is due by November 16, 2027; no individual record should be assumed sealed yet.

evidence.value: Misdemeanors sealed after three years and most felonies after eight years without new convictions; parole or probation must be finished.
evidence.limitations: Secondary plain-language summary; the statute is CPL 160.57. Statewide legal-information site; page last reviewed May 7, 2025. Used for the Legal Action Center referral and plain-language waiting periods only.

evidence.value: Certification for any condition the provider deems suitable; purchases up to a 60-day supply or 3 oz/24 g, whichever is greater; certification may be issued for less than two years; patients and caregivers 18+ may grow at home.
evidence.limitations: Program instructions. Individual eligibility is decided by the certifying provider. Product availability and prices are set by registered organizations.

rules.summary: Adults 21+ may grow up to six plants per person and twelve at one residence, subject to secured-area, primary-residence and other statutory conditions.
An application-based process for specified marijuana/hashish possession cases before March 20, 2026. Eligibility and court procedures are stated in the statute.

Medical use is lawful only under the Medical Marijuana Act: a registered patient or caregiver with a Department of Health ID card and practitioner certification. A dispensary may not dispense more than a 90-day supply. Smoking medical marijuana is unlawful; patients and caregivers may make edibles themselves.

Pennsylvania has no adult-use (recreational) cannabis law. Without a medical card, possessing up to 30 grams of marijuana or 8 grams of hashish for personal use is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 30 days in jail, a fine of up to $500, or both. Some cities have their own ordinances; this summary covers state law only.

Home cultivation is not allowed. Only grower/processors permitted by the Department of Health may grow medical marijuana, and Pennsylvania has no adult-use home-grow law. Growing hemp requires a separate Department of Agriculture permit.

An employer may not fire, refuse to hire or otherwise discriminate against someone solely because they are certified to use medical marijuana. Employers need not allow use at work and may discipline employees for being under the influence at work when their conduct falls below the standard of care for the job.

Driving with any amount of a Schedule I controlled substance or its metabolite in your blood is DUI, whether or not you are impaired. Marijuana is a Schedule I substance under Pennsylvania law, and the DUI statute has no exception for medical marijuana patients.

Clean Slate limits access to (seals) certain records automatically: charges that did not end in a conviction; summary convictions after five years; and second- and third-degree misdemeanors and misdemeanors punishable by up to two years after seven years free of convictions punishable by a year or more. Court-ordered restitution must be paid. A pardon is a separate step.

Adults 21 and older may possess, buy and transport up to 3 ounces of cannabis and 24 grams of concentrated cannabis, and may give the same amounts to another adult 21 or older without compensation. At home, up to 5 pounds may be kept if secured from anyone under 21. 'Gifting' tied to a sale is not lawful sharing.

Adults may consume in a private home and most places where tobacco smoking is allowed, but not in a motor vehicle, where smoking or vaping is banned, on school grounds or school buses, or on federal property. Violations of the state use restrictions carry a civil penalty of up to $25 or up to 20 hours of community service.

Adults 21 and older may grow up to 3 mature and 3 immature plants, with no more than 6 mature and 6 immature plants per residence, only at their private residence and secured from anyone under 21. Selling homegrown cannabis is illegal, and flammable solvents are banned for home processing. Localities may regulate but not effectively ban home growing.

Employers generally may not act against workers for lawful off-duty cannabis use away from the workplace and without employer property. Employers may still act when required by state or federal law, when a worker shows specific articulable signs of impairment on the job, or when allowing it would violate federal law or risk a federal contract or funding.

Driving while impaired by a drug, or by drugs combined with alcohol, is a crime and is treated like alcohol-impaired driving. Cannabis in a vehicle must be in a closed container, and smoking cannabis in a vehicle is illegal for drivers and passengers.

Convictions under the listed marijuana offenses (possession up to 16 ounces or sale up to 25 grams) are expunged automatically, with no motion or fee and no notice sent. Expunged cases do not appear on background checks and need not be disclosed. Other marijuana convictions require a CPL 440.46-a motion.

The Clean Slate Act provides automatic sealing of eligible convictions for certain civil background checks: misdemeanors after three years and most felonies after eight years without new convictions. Courts have until November 16, 2027 to finish setting it up. Sex crimes and non-drug Class A felonies are not eligible.

A New York certifying provider may certify a patient for any condition the provider judges suitable. Patients or caregivers may buy up to a 60-day supply or 3 ounces of cannabis or 24 grams of concentrate, whichever is greater, and certifications may run up to two years. S3294A, signed in 2025, also lets registered patients and caregivers 18 and older grow at home and lets patients certified in other states buy here.

Adults 21+ may use and possess marijuana bought from a licensed Ohio dispensary. The total amount a person may possess, counting dispensary and homegrown marijuana together, is 2.5 ounces of plant material and 15 grams of extract. An adult may give the same amounts to another adult in a single day, without payment, only on private residential or agricultural property; other transfers require a license.

Using adult-use or homegrown marijuana in a public place is prohibited, and the person running a public place may not knowingly allow it. Use is legal at a private residence, subject to the property owner's rules.

Neither the adult-use nor the medical marijuana law allows driving (or operating a streetcar, watercraft or aircraft) under the influence of marijuana. Ohio's OVI law also makes it an offense to drive with marijuana or marijuana metabolite at or above set concentrations in blood or urine, whether or not impairment is shown. Medical registration is not a defense.

Ohio's marijuana law does not require employers to allow or accommodate marijuana use, possession or distribution. Employers may refuse to hire, discharge or discipline someone because of marijuana use, and may keep drug-testing, drug-free workplace and zero-tolerance policies. This applies to medical and adult-use marijuana alike.

A patient registered with the Division of Cannabis Control, with a recommendation from a certified physician for a qualifying condition, may use and possess medical marijuana bought from a licensed dispensary, up to a 90-day supply as set by rule. Caregivers register separately. Patients may not drive under the influence.

location_source.description: These are the 200 locations on the Pennsylvania Department of Health roster of medical marijuana dispensaries with product, dated September 16, 2026 and retrieved October 28, 2026. The roster lists no permit numbers or counties. County and map points come from the U.S. Census Bureau Geocoder where it matched the exact address (163 of 200). Confirm hours, products and patient requirements with the store and the Department of Health.

pathways.next_step: Search the 200 Department of Health roster locations by city, county or distance, then confirm details with the store.
pathways.limitations: Denominator: all 200 rows of the Department of Health roster dated September 16, 2026. The roster is not a live permit list and names no permit holder. Store brands are grouped by the name printed on the roster, not by ownership. 37 locations have no county or map point because the Census geocoder did not match their exact address.

pathways.next_step: Read the home-cultivation rule; hemp growers can apply for a Department of Agriculture permit.
pathways.limitations: Home cultivation of cannabis is not allowed in Pennsylvania, so no seed sellers are listed. The one route is the Department of Agriculture hemp permit for licensed hemp growing.

pathways.next_step: Check what Clean Slate seals automatically, get your record, then use a local legal-help route or the Board of Pardons.
pathways.limitations: Statewide record access, pardon and verification tools plus selected regional legal-aid, county self-help and referral routes. MidPenn, Northwestern Legal Services, Neighborhood Legal Services and Summit now have reviewed service pages describing record barriers or relief. Service areas, income limits, matter eligibility and capacity vary; county forms, legal aid, paid referrals and pardon coaching are distinct. No individual representation or automatic cannabis relief is established. Historical or unverified court leads remain in research.

pathways.next_step: Read each dated summary, then the official statute it cites.
pathways.limitations: Six state-law summaries checked October 28, 2026 against the General Assembly's statute text: medical use limits, adult-use status and small-amount possession, home cultivation, employment protection, driving and Clean Slate sealing. Not legal advice. Local ordinances, hemp-derived products, Department of Health regulations and court orders are not summarized.

pathways.next_step: Register, find an approved practitioner, then check caregiver, fee and assistance options.
pathways.limitations: Official registration, approved-practitioner, caregiver and assistance routes plus provider-stated evaluation, education, peer support and conditional subsidy resources. No individual clinician license or program approval, appointment, fee, subsidy slot or medical outcome was independently verified. Paid clinical evaluation is separate from state registration. Read the source conditions before applying.

pathways.next_step: Choose testing, legal, accounting, security, insurance, banking, payments, packaging, equipment, training or hemp resources, then confirm the engagement scope.
pathways.limitations: Selected Pennsylvania-relevant sources now include packaging, extraction equipment, software integration documentation, professional services, training and industrial-hemp resources alongside the baseline operators and laboratories. This is not a complete current permit roster or provider census. Office presence does not establish statewide service. Hemp resources are separate from medical-marijuana licensing; listing does not verify credentials, regulatory compliance or availability.

pathways.next_step: Contact a group about meetings, membership or advocacy.
pathways.limitations: Selected groups, peer networks, education programs, research resources and advocacy contacts. No Pennsylvania cannabis events are verified for the next three months. A recurring program or completed demonstration does not establish an upcoming event, open enrollment or current grant. Confirm membership, admissions and participation directly.

pathways.next_step: Search the 698 OCM-licensed adult-use stores and 24 open medical dispensing facilities by city, county, ZIP or distance, then confirm details with the store.
pathways.limitations: Denominator: every row of the OCM Current OCM Licenses export of November 1, 2026 with Active license and operational status, retail sales purpose and an opening date (698 of 3,040 rows), plus the 24 of 30 OCM medical dispensing facilities not marked temporarily closed. A licensing snapshot, not a live license check. Approximate Census map points for 644 of 722 locations (geocoded November 1, 2026); 78 addresses had no exact match or a county that disagreed with the regulator's and have no map point. 11 registered-organization adult-use sites with no opening date are not included.

pathways.next_step: Read the home-grow rule, then call a licensed dispensary, microbusiness or registered organization to ask whether it sells seeds or immature plants.
pathways.limitations: Sources reviewed November 1, 2026. Adults 21+ may grow 3 mature and 3 immature plants (6 and 6 per residence); registered patients and caregivers 18+ may grow for a patient. OCM names licensed retailers, microbusinesses and registered organizations as seed and plant sources, but no store-level seed or plant availability has been reviewed, and no online or mail-order supplier has been reviewed for New York shipping.

pathways.next_step: Check whether a marijuana conviction was expunged automatically, see where Clean Slate sealing stands, or apply for CPL 160.59 sealing; free legal help is listed statewide and for New York City, Syracuse and Rochester.
pathways.limitations: Sources reviewed November 1, 2026. Statewide court routes for automatic marijuana expungement, the CPL 440.46-a motion, CPL 160.59 sealing and Clean Slate status, plus legal help that its own pages say covers sealing or record correction: Legal Action Center (statewide phone), The Legal Aid Society's Case Closed (New York City convictions), Community Service Society's Next Door Project and Youth Represent (New York City), The Bronx Defenders and Brooklyn Defender Services, and the Center for Community Alternatives (Syracuse and Rochester). Long Island, the Hudson Valley, the Capital Region, the North Country and Western New York outside Rochester have no listed regional route yet: LawNY, the Legal Aid Society of Northeastern New York and the Legal Aid Bureau of Buffalo were checked and their pages do not say they handle sealing. Clean Slate implementation is due by November 16, 2027, so no record should be assumed sealed. Not legal advice.

pathways.next_step: Read the dated summaries and the statute text each one links to.
pathways.limitations: Sources reviewed November 1, 2026. Eight summaries checked against statute text or official pages: possession and sharing, consumption, home cultivation, employment, driving, marijuana expungement, Clean Slate sealing and medical use. Not legal advice. Local rules, landlord and co-op policies, hemp-derived products, packaging and business rules are not summarized. The S3294A medical changes are summarized from OCM and the bill page; the chapter number and each provision's effective date were not confirmed.

pathways.next_step: Find a certifying provider, get certified, then buy at a medical dispensing facility with your certification and photo ID.
pathways.limitations: Sources reviewed November 1, 2026. Official certification, provider-finder, caregiver, home-grow and dispensing-facility routes. 69,031 registered patients and 4,820 certifying practitioners as of October 1, 2026 (OCM). Provider rows, appointment fees, product prices and registered-organization discounts were not reviewed. Out-of-state patient purchases under S3294A are not yet confirmed as in effect.

pathways.next_step: Find an OCM-permitted testing laboratory or approved sampling firm, a bank from OCM's cannabis banking directory, or use OCM licensing for applications and permits.
pathways.limitations: Sources reviewed November 1, 2026. Regulator-published lists: all 11 OCM-permitted testing laboratories with their testing scope, all 13 OCM-approved sampling firms, and the 20 banks and credit unions in OCM's Cannabis Banking Directory with the regions and services each lists (OCM says the directory is not an endorsement). Plus OCM licensing routes. Insurance, legal, accounting, security, packaging, technology and other providers have not been reviewed for New York service. The adult-use licensees in the location finder are reference records, not reviewed business listings. Trade associations remain leads; the CANY site could not be opened on November 1, 2026.

pathways.next_step: Contact a NORML chapter about meetings or advocacy, or register for the OCM clinical symposium.
pathways.limitations: Sources reviewed November 1, 2026. Three NORML chapters from NORML's national listing and one OCM event (November 19-20, 2026, Tarrytown). Chapter activity was not confirmed on the chapters' own sites. Trade associations, veteran groups and other events have not been reviewed.

location_source.description: These are the 698 stores in the Office of Cannabis Management's Current OCM Licenses open-data export (retrieved November 1, 2026) whose license and operational status are both Active, whose business purpose includes retail sales and that have a date opened to the public, plus the 24 medical dispensing facilities on OCM's medical list that are not marked temporarily closed. County comes from the regulator. Map points for 644 of the 722 locations come from the U.S. Census Bureau Geocoder where it matched the exact address and the regulator's county; the rest are listed after locations with distances. The adult-use export has no phone numbers. Confirm hours, products and delivery with the store.
location_source.count_note: OCM's dispensary verification page states 757 adult-use dispensaries (no as-of date). The export's 698 active, opened stores leave out 11 registered-organization adult-use sites that have no opening date and 53 retail rows with an opening date that are marked non-operational (39 with an active license, 14 inactive). The remaining difference is unreconciled. OCM's medical list has 30 facilities; the 6 marked temporarily closed are not shown.

items.description: Statewide explanation of sealing, expungement and legal-aid options. Start here to identify the right assistance for your county.

items.name: Eligibility interview and action plan
items.description: A guided record-sealing interview that produces next steps. Have your court names, case numbers and charge details ready. This general tool is separate from the marijuana-specific statute below.

items.name: Opportunity Port
items.description: Currently serves Franklin County residents seeking help with Ohio records. Legal assistance is free; filing fees may apply. Services outside Franklin County are paused.

items.name: Marijuana-specific expungement: ORC 2953.321
items.description: Effective March 20, 2026. Covers specified marijuana/hashish possession cases from before that date, including certain dismissed cases. Apply to the sentencing court with case information and evidence of the covered offense. Relief requires a court process; it is not automatic. The statute sets a $50 application fee unless indigent.

items.name: Urban Expungement Program (Hamilton County)
items.description: Free legal support and record-clearing help for eligible cases, with record reviews, help with paperwork and court filings, and help toward eligible fees. Run with the Hamilton County Public Defender's Office, the Ohio Justice Bus and the Hamilton County Clerk of Courts Help Center. Watch the page for the next clinic date.

items.description: Official steps for obtaining a recommendation, registering and purchasing medical cannabis. Bring an active registry card, active recommendation and government-issued ID when purchasing.

items.description: For registry questions, the state publishes 1-833-464-6627 and MMCPRegistry@com.ohio.gov. Choose patient and caregiver resources on the DCC page.

items.name: Find a physician certified to recommend
items.description: Only an Ohio physician holding an active certificate to recommend (CTR) from the State Medical Board of Ohio can recommend medical marijuana. The board's CTR search finds certified physicians by practice location. Questions: medicalmarijuana@med.ohio.gov.

items.name: Home growing: ORC 3796.04
items.description: Adults 21+ may grow up to six plants per person, with no more than twelve at one residence. Grow at your primary residence in a secured enclosed area, inaccessible to people under 21 and not visible from public space. Rental prohibitions and other residence restrictions apply. The section prohibits selling homegrown marijuana, hydrocarbon extraction and public consumption.

items.description: Read the current law for possession, transport, purchase, patient and other requirements. Home-growing permission does not answer every possession or transport question.
